title: Pdi1 residue library: which residues drive ribosome binding
objective: Identify which residues of the wasp proline-rich antimicrobial peptide Pdi1 drive its binding to the bacterial ribosome, separating binding determinants from determinants of uptake and potency.
coordinate_note: Pdi1 numbering, 1-20 (UniProt C0HKX8). Across the conserved C-terminal PRPPHPRL (Pdi1 13-20) apidaecin 1b numbering is Pdi1 minus 2, so Pdi1 Arg19 = Api Arg17. Upstream of that the Pdi1/Api alignment has no unique solution: Pdi1 has a two-residue longer N-terminus and Pdi1 Pro10-Ile11 are transposed relative to Api Ile8-Pro9. Only literature dated before 2026-01-01 was used.

regions.name: N-terminal leader
regions.description: Glycine-lysine-proline start and first cationic residues. Unresolved in every Api-type ribosome structure; mutation-tolerant in Api; correlated with potency and charge. Contacts for this part of Api137 are reported at a second, exit-pore site.

regions.name: Central tunnel segment
regions.description: Residues that are resolved in the tunnel in Api/Fva1 structures and lie between the leader and the conserved pharmacophore. Sequence differs most between Pdi1, Api and Fva1.

regions.name: C-terminal pharmacophore
regions.description: The eight-residue Pro-Arg-Pro-Pro-His-Pro-Arg-Leu segment conserved across Api-like peptides, placed identically near the peptidyl transferase centre in the Api, Api137 and Fva1 structures.

regions.name: Release-factor and tRNA contact terminus
regions.description: The terminal Arg-Leu pair: Arg contacts the release-factor Gln of the GGQ motif and rRNA; the C-terminal carboxylate contacts the 3' end of the P-site tRNA and the GGQ backbone.

hypotheses.question: Which residues of the conserved C-terminal pharmacophore carry Pdi1's binding to the post-release ribosome, and how much does each contribute?
hypotheses.mechanism: In the Api, Api137 and Fva1 structures the identical eight-residue segment contacts 23S rRNA (His stacking on G2505, backbone hydrogen bond to A2062), the release-factor GGQ glutamine (Arg) and the P-site tRNA 3' end (carboxylate). Each residue is therefore expected to contribute through its own contact. An alanine scan removes one side chain at a time and keeps length and register.
hypotheses.measurement: Affinity (competition fluorescence polarisation against a labelled tracer, or biolayer interferometry) of each variant for 70S ribosomes in the defined post-release state (stop codon, RF1 or RF2, deacylated P-site tRNA), relative to Pdi1 in the same plate. Orthogonal readout: toeprint stall at the stop codon with RF1, which reports the PTC-proximal site. Uptake check: MIC in wild type versus a delta-sbmA strain.
hypotheses.note: Pro13 and Pro15 are deferred to a second round (no residue-specific contact reported for them in the structures read). Cell-based activity alone cannot separate binding from uptake.

hypotheses.question: Does the free C-terminal carboxylate, as distinct from the Leu20 side chain, set how Pdi1 binds and whether it traps the release factor?
hypotheses.mechanism: The carboxylate sits within hydrogen-bond distance of the A76 ribose hydroxyls of the P-site tRNA and the GGQ backbone NH. Amidating the Api137 terminus (Api88) is reported to shift the peptide deeper into the tunnel, make it more dynamic, add a third binding pocket and reduce RF-dependent inhibition, so the terminal group may select a binding mode as well as add an affinity term.
hypotheses.measurement: Affinity on 70S with RF1 and deacylated tRNA versus on vacant 70S and on isolated 50S; stop-codon toeprint with RF1. Read against the Leu20 side-chain variant, which removes the side chain and keeps the carboxylate.
hypotheses.note: This construct changes charge as well as the carboxylate itself (+5 to +6).

hypotheses.question: Is Pdi1 binding confined to its C-terminal segment (Api-like), or do its N-terminal cationic residues also contribute, as reported for drosocin?
hypotheses.mechanism: In drosocin, which also starts Gly-Lys-Pro, Lys2, Arg4 and Arg9 are pivotal and important residues are spread through the peptide, whereas Api's N-terminal segment is disordered in structures and tolerant of substitution. Pdi1 combines a drosocin-like start with an Api-like C-terminus. Neutralising the leader's cationic residues tests whether they bind, as against only aiding uptake.
hypotheses.measurement: Affinity on the defined post-release 70S and on isolated 50S, plus toeprint stall, against the reference; MIC in wild type versus delta-sbmA. Unchanged binding with a higher MIC points to uptake; weaker binding points to distributed binding and justifies single substitutions.
hypotheses.note: A three-residue block is used on purpose as a first cut. It lowers net charge from +5 to +2, which is itself a confound.

hypotheses.question: Does the absence of an aromatic residue at the Pdi1 position equivalent to Api Tyr7 limit Pdi1's tunnel binding?
hypotheses.mechanism: In Api137, Tyr7 stacks between rRNA bases A751 side-on (a candidate anchor in the upper tunnel) and is also wedged between A91 and A92 at the exit-pore site. Fva1 has a tyrosine in the equivalent column, whereas Pdi1 has alanine. Restoring the ring tests whether Pdi1 lacks this anchor or uses another contact.
hypotheses.measurement: Dissociation rate and affinity on the defined post-release 70S relative to the reference; toeprint stall with RF1.
hypotheses.note: Equivalence of position 9 to Api Tyr7 rests on an ungapped C-terminal anchored alignment; Pdi1 Pro10-Ile11 and Api Ile8-Pro9 are transposed.

omitted.reason: Deferred to a second round to keep the opening library interpretable; no residue-specific contact for the equivalent Api Pro11 is reported in the structures read, and its cell-based effects are confounded with uptake.
Deferred to a second round for the same reasons; equivalent Api Pro13 is described as forgiving in vivo and as an exit-pore stacking site, which this round does not resolve.

series.coverage: Six of the eight positions of the conserved C-terminal segment. Positions 13 and 15 are prolines deferred to a second round.

sites.label: Arg19 — release-factor and rRNA anchor

observations.finding: The Arg17 side chain of Api137 is fixed by hydrogen bonds to the 2' hydroxyl of the G2505 ribose and O2 of C2452, and sits within hydrogen-bond distance of the RF1 Gln235 side chain.
observations.context: Cryo-EM, 3.4 Å, E. coli 70S with RF1 and P-site tRNA, Api137 present.

observations.finding: Replacing Arg17 of Api137 with homoarginine or citrulline raised the MIC 16-fold and 128-fold, and N-methylating its backbone amide raised it 67-fold; a mono-methylated side chain kept full activity.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivatives, E. coli MIC.

observations.finding: Arg17 was almost never altered among active Api variants recovered from a library of about 350,000 multiply substituted peptides.
observations.context: Endogenous expression in E. coli with depletion selection.

sites.note: Api numbering 17 = Pdi1 19, fixed by the identical C-terminal PRPPHPRL. Gln235 is E. coli RF1 numbering; the T. thermophilus RF1 residue in the Fva1 structure is Gln230.

sites.label: Leu20 and C-terminal carboxylate — P-site tRNA contact

observations.finding: The carboxylate oxygens of the terminal Leu are 3.1 and 3.4 Å from the 2' and 3' hydroxyls of tRNA A76. A decarboxy-Leu Api137 was inactive (MIC above 40 µM), and amino-alcohol replacements raised the MIC 32-fold or more.
observations.context: Cryo-EM geometry plus synthetic Api137 derivatives, E. coli MIC.

observations.finding: In the Fva1 structure one carboxylate oxygen is within hydrogen-bond distance of the A76 2' and 3' hydroxyls and the other hydrogen-bonds the main-chain NH of the GGQ glutamine of RF1.
observations.context: X-ray, 2.7 Å, T. thermophilus 70S with RF1 and deacylated tRNA-Phe.

observations.finding: An earlier genetic study is summarised as placing the pharmacophore in the five C-terminal residues, with the last position tolerating any residue except Ala, Ser or Gly.
observations.context: Secondary citation of Baliga 2021.

sites.label: His17 — stacking on rRNA G2505

observations.finding: His15 forms pi-pi stacking with the G2505 base. Naphthylalanine, cyclohexylalanine or tryptophan at this position raised the MIC 8 to 64-fold, so the pocket does not take a larger side chain.
observations.context: Cryo-EM geometry plus synthetic Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: Replacing Pro14 or His15 with tyrosine remained compatible with activity of the endogenously expressed peptide, interpreted as retaining the stacking.
observations.context: Multi-substitution Api library, E. coli.

observations.finding: At the second, exit-pore site the His15 side chain extends back to Pro11 and stabilises the peptide intramolecularly.
observations.context: Cryo-EM of 50S with Api137.

sites.note: Api numbering 15 = Pdi1 17. The Skowron paper numbers the nucleotide G2505; one extraction of Baliga 2021 reads A2505, which is treated as an extraction error.

sites.label: Pro16 — rRNA proximity and backbone geometry

observations.finding: A thioamide at Pro14 raised the MIC 125-fold, the largest effect of any proline, although the Pro14 carbonyl was not seen to contact tunnel elements.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivatives, E. coli MIC.

observations.finding: Mutations of 23S rRNA nucleotides 2059 and 2503, near this part of the peptide, made cells resistant to Api137 and abolished its stop-codon arrest of the mutant ribosomes in vitro.
observations.context: E. coli resistance mutants and toeprinting.

observations.finding: Fluoroproline substitutions at Pro14 and Pro16 had the strongest effects on in vitro translation inhibition and on 50S-assembly effects, and were interpreted as conformer-dependent.
observations.context: E. coli 70S, fluorescence polarisation competition, sfGFP in vitro translation.

sites.note: Api numbering 14 = Pdi1 16. Sources disagree on whether this proline contacts rRNA directly: one reports contact with A2059 and A2503, another reports none for the carbonyl.

sites.label: Pro18 — positions the terminal Arg-Leu pair

observations.finding: The cis/trans state of the bond preceding Pro16 was argued to determine where Arg17 and Leu18 sit at the PTC; the 4R-fluoroproline analogue bound best (Ki 0.78 nM versus 2.6 nM for Api137) and the 4S analogue worse (4.8 nM).
observations.context: E. coli 70S, fluorescence polarisation competition against labelled Api137.

observations.finding: At the exit-pore site Pro16 is potentially stacked on A1321.
observations.context: Cryo-EM of 50S with Api137.

observations.finding: A thioamide at Pro16 raised the MIC four-fold.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivative.

sites.label: Arg14 — invariant arginine of the pharmacophore

observations.finding: Pro11 and Arg12 (like Arg17 and Leu18) were almost never altered among active Api variants, attributed by the authors to contacts with tunnel elements.
observations.context: Endogenous expression in E. coli with depletion selection.

observations.finding: The eight-residue segment PRPPHPRL is conserved across the 71 Api-like peptides identified in bee and wasp genomes.
observations.context: Genome mining and alignment.

sites.note: No structural paper read describes a specific contact for this Arg; its role is inferred from invariance and from the general Arg/His/Tyr pi-stacking pattern. Api numbering 12 = Pdi1 14.

sites.label: Ala9 — column of Api Tyr7, which stacks on A751

observations.finding: Tyr7 of Api137 makes a pi-pi sandwich with the A751 base; para-fluoro-Phe kept full activity (0.35 µM), cyclohexylalanine cost two-fold and para-methoxy-Phe four-fold.
observations.context: Cryo-EM geometry plus synthetic Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: A751 is proposed as an initial anchor in the upper tunnel, and at the second site Tyr7 is wedged between A91 and A92.
observations.context: Cryo-EM and MD.

observations.finding: Fva1, which has a tyrosine in this column, was among the most potent peptides, and the authors favour better uptake over higher ribosome affinity as the reason.
observations.context: Comparison of Api, Fva1 and others.

sites.note: This site marks a missing contact: Pdi1 has Ala where Api has Tyr. The column assignment rests on an ungapped C-terminal anchored alignment, and Api Ile8-Pro9 is transposed relative to Pdi1 Pro10-Ile11.

sites.label: Lys2 and Arg5 — leader cations, drosocin-like

observations.finding: Any substitution of drosocin Lys2, Arg4 or Arg9, including with another cationic residue, reduced activity of the expressed peptide, and important residues were reported to be distributed through the peptide.
observations.context: Saturation mutagenesis of endogenously expressed non-glycosylated drosocin in E. coli.

observations.finding: Net charge of +4 to +6 and a one or two residue N-terminal extension correlated with higher potency among Api-like peptides, and the authors attribute this to SbmA uptake because these regions are dispensable for ribosome binding.
observations.context: MIC and charge comparison of the 26 peptides.

sites.note: Transfer from drosocin by alignment of the shared Gly-Lys-Pro start; Pdi1 has one extra residue (Asn4) relative to drosocin, so drosocin Arg4 maps to Pdi1 Arg5. Drosocin is otherwise only distantly related to Pdi1.

sites.label: Arg7 — first tunnel residue, candidate drosocin Arg9 counterpart
sites.note: Inference by the author of this record: Pdi1 Pro6-Arg7-Pro8 has the spacing of drosocin Pro8-Arg9-Pro10, and Arg7 is the first residue within the modelled Api/Fva1 chain. No source maps this residue; the alignment between Pdi1 and drosocin is not defined here.

attempted_analyses.reason: The UniRef50 cluster of C0HKX8 holds 3 sequences, all Pimpla disparis apidaecin paralogs, below the floor of 30, and the entry carries no Pfam family, so there is no family-level fallback. Conservation over three near-identical paralogs would carry no independent evidence.
attempted_analyses.attempted: fetch_homologs.py C0HKX8 against rest.uniprot.org, default ortholog level; refused at the floor of 30. Family conservation of the C-terminal PRPPHPRL across 71 Api-like peptides is reported in Huang 2024 and is cited as literature, not computed here.

precedent_search.scope: Europe PMC search and forward citations to 2025-12-31 of Huang 2024 (EMBO Rep), Baliga 2021, Skowron 2023 and Florin 2017, UniProt, and web search, for prior alanine, saturation or structure-guided scans of Type II proline-rich peptides and for any residue-level study of Pdi1. Completed before the constructs were chosen. No pre-2026 Pdi1 residue scan was found. A Pdi1 ribosome-binding study dated after the cutoff is indexed and was excluded; only its title and abstract snippet were seen in search results.

variants.name: Pdi1 (reference)
variants.note: Native 20-residue Apidaecin 1+ of Pimpla disparis (UniProt C0HKX8), as free acid. The natural processed 1- form lacks residues 1-3.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: Comparator for every variant. Its ribosome-arresting activity is measured, but the contribution of each residue to binding is not.

observations.finding: Synthetic Pdi1 inhibited E. coli BL21 at 0.125 µM in 33% TSB and 1 µM in RPMI/serum, against 0.5 and 4 µM for Api, and K. pneumoniae AR-0112 at 1 and 16 µM; it was among the most potent peptides tested.
observations.context: Broth microdilution of the synthetic peptide.

observations.finding: Pdi1 produced a stop-codon toeprint like Api and Api137 and a GFP stop-codon readthrough halo, the two hallmarks of release-factor trapping.
observations.context: PURExpress toeprinting on a yrbA template and the pRXG(UGA) reporter in E. coli BL21.

observations.finding: The peptide was isolated from the hemolymph of P. disparis as a 20-residue form and a 17-residue form lacking the first three residues, with different activity spectra.
observations.context: Protein sequencing and MALDI mass spectrometry, as curated by UniProt.

rationale.comparison: Run on the same plate and ribosome preparation as each variant.
rationale.uncertainty: No pre-2026 study measures which Pdi1 residues bind the ribosome. Every residue-level role used here is transferred from Api, Api137, Fva1 or drosocin, and the Pdi1 sequence differs from Api between positions 3 and 12.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: The arginine invariant across Api-like peptides contributes to tunnel binding independently of the release-factor-bridging Arg19.
rationale.edit: Removes the pharmacophore's second arginine while keeping length, prolines and the terminal pair.

observations.finding: Pro11 and Arg12 were nearly invariant among active Api variants, attributed to tunnel-element contacts.
observations.context: Endogenous expression in E. coli with depletion selection.

observations.finding: PRPPHPRL is conserved across 71 Api-like peptides.
observations.context: Genome mining and alignment.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference for the contribution of Arg14. Against R19A to separate a tunnel Arg from the release-factor Arg.
rationale.uncertainty: No structure read assigns a specific contact to this arginine, so a loss may be general electrostatics (net charge +5 to +4) rather than a defined contact. Arg14 is followed by Pro15, so the Arg-Pro bond that resists trypsin is removed too.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: Pro16 contributes through backbone geometry and proximity to rRNA 2059 and 2503, not through a side chain.
rationale.edit: Replaces a proline with alanine, which adds a backbone NH and relaxes the polyproline-II constraint at this site.

observations.finding: A thioamide at the equivalent Api Pro14 raised the MIC 125-fold although its carbonyl was not seen to contact the tunnel.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: Replacing the equivalent Pro14 with tyrosine remained compatible with activity of the expressed peptide.
observations.context: Multi-substitution Api library.

observations.finding: Fluoroproline at the equivalent Pro14 changed in vitro translation inhibition depending on the epimer, which was read as conformer dependence.
observations.context: E. coli 70S, sfGFP in vitro translation.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference and against P18A, the other proline immediately upstream of the terminal pair.
rationale.uncertainty: A change in binding may reflect altered cis/trans behaviour of the preceding Pro15-Pro16 bond and conformational spread to His17-Leu20, not loss of a contact at residue 16. Sources disagree on whether the equivalent Api proline touches rRNA.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: His17 stacks on 23S rRNA G2505 and its removal weakens binding more than any proline change.
rationale.edit: Removes the imidazole ring that stacks on the rRNA base.

observations.finding: His15 stacks on G2505; large aromatic replacements raised the MIC 8 to 64-fold.
observations.context: Cryo-EM geometry and synthetic Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: His15 to tyrosine remained compatible with activity of the expressed peptide.
observations.context: Multi-substitution Api library.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference. A later aromatic replacement such as Tyr would separate ring loss from loss of the imidazole specifically.
rationale.uncertainty: His15 also contributes at the second, exit-pore site, so a loss on bulk 70S binding cannot be assigned to the tunnel site alone. Histidine is partly protonated near neutral pH, so buffer pH changes the readout.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: Pro18 sets the register of the terminal Arg-Leu pair, and its removal weakens the PTC-proximal contacts.
rationale.edit: Replaces the proline directly before the terminal pair with alanine.

observations.finding: The cis/trans state of the bond before the equivalent Pro16 changed binding affinity (Ki 0.78 versus 4.8 nM) and was argued to reposition Arg17 and Leu18.
observations.context: E. coli 70S, competition fluorescence polarisation.

observations.finding: A thioamide at Pro16 raised the MIC four-fold.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivative.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference and against R19A and L20A: a loss that exceeds R19A or L20A alone would point to loss of terminal register, since those two remove the contacts directly.
rationale.uncertainty: Alanine changes backbone torsions at residue 18 and leaves the H17-A18 bond free to adopt either isomer, so an effect may not reflect any contact at residue 18.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: Isolates binding that depends on the Arg-GGQ and rRNA anchoring contact: the residue whose every tested replacement inactivates Api-type peptides.
rationale.edit: Removes the penultimate arginine that contacts the release-factor glutamine.

observations.finding: Arg17 side chain hydrogen-bonds G2505 ribose and C2452, positioned to contact RF1 Gln235.
observations.context: Cryo-EM of Api137 with E. coli 70S and RF1.

observations.finding: Homoarginine, citrulline and backbone N-methylation at Arg17 raised the MIC 16 to 128-fold.
observations.context: Synthetic Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: Arg17 was almost never altered among active Api variants.
observations.context: Library selection in E. coli.

rationale.comparison: Anchors the loss end of the scan. A variant that binds like R19A loses its dependence on the release factor.
rationale.uncertainty: A binding-defective Arg variant is not assumed inert: it keeps the rest of the cationic, proline-rich peptide, so residual association with the 70S, particularly at the exit-pore site, may remain.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: The Leu20 side chain, as distinct from the terminal carboxylate, is needed for stable placement of the C-terminus at the PTC.
rationale.edit: Shortens the terminal side chain to a methyl group while keeping the free carboxylate.

observations.finding: The genetic pharmacophore is summarised as allowing any residue at the last position except Ala, Ser or Gly.
observations.context: Secondary citation of Baliga 2021.

observations.finding: The terminal carboxylate hydrogen-bonds the A76 hydroxyls and the GGQ backbone NH.
observations.context: X-ray structure of Fva1 with RF1 and tRNA.

rationale.comparison: Against the C-terminal amide, which changes the carboxylate and keeps Leu, so the pair separates the side chain from the terminal group.
rationale.uncertainty: The source for the Ala/Ser/Gly exclusion is a secondary citation, and the Leu contacts in the PTC pocket are not defined in the structures read.

variants.name: Pdi1 C-terminal amide
variants.headline: C-terminal carboxamide
variants.note: Same letters as the reference; the C-terminal carboxylic acid is replaced by a primary amide.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

caps.note: C-terminal amide in place of the free carboxylic acid.

rationale.hypothesis: Removing the terminal negative charge changes the binding mode, and possibly release-factor trapping, independently of the Leu20 side chain.
rationale.edit: Replaces the terminal carboxylic acid with a primary amide. A chemistry change has no edit form.

observations.finding: Amidated Api88 was positioned 3.2 Å deeper than Api137, adopted at least three conformers, occupied a third binding pocket in 23S rRNA domain III, and inhibited translation largely independently of RF1 and about 50% less effectively than Api137 with RF1.
observations.context: Cryo-EM of 50S and 70S, fluorescence polarisation on purified 70S, in vitro translation.

observations.finding: Purified 70S bound labelled Api137 with Kd 4.7 µM and Api88 with Kd 1.8 µM.
observations.context: Fluorescence polarisation, E. coli 70S purified to remove release-factor carry-over.

observations.finding: Api137 showed antibacterial activity very similar to the amidated Api88.
observations.context: E. coli MIC.

observations.finding: Removing the carboxyl group altogether (decarboxy-Leu) made Api137 inactive.
observations.context: Synthetic derivative, E. coli MIC.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference for the terminal group, and against L20A for the side chain. Binding on vacant 70S versus RF-bound 70S distinguishes a lost A76/GGQ contact from a changed mode.
rationale.uncertainty: Amidation also raises net charge by one, so a change in 70S binding may reflect electrostatics and the third site rather than loss of the A76 hydrogen bond. The data for this effect are for an apidaecin with different N-terminal chemistry (N-terminal guanidino-ornithine), not for Pdi1.

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: If binding is distributed, as for drosocin, neutralising the leader's cations weakens binding; if it is C-terminal only, as for Api, binding is unchanged and only uptake changes.
rationale.edit: Replaces the three cationic residues upstream of the conserved segment with alanine, keeping length and the prolines.

observations.finding: Substituting drosocin Lys2, Arg4 or Arg9, even with another cationic residue, lowered activity, and important residues were spread across the peptide.
observations.context: Saturation mutagenesis of expressed non-glycosylated drosocin.

observations.finding: The Api and Fva1 N-terminal segments were not resolved in the electron density, and the authors attribute charge and extension effects on potency to uptake.
observations.context: X-ray structures of ribosome complexes; MIC panel.

observations.finding: At the exit-pore site Api137 residues Asn3, Val6, Tyr7 and Arg10 contact rRNA, so the leader may bind there.
observations.context: Cryo-EM of 50S with Api137.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference for binding and MIC separately, so uptake and binding can be read apart.
rationale.uncertainty: Three substitutions lower net charge from +5 to +2, so a binding loss could be nonspecific electrostatics. Arg7 is the first residue in the modelled chain, so it may belong to the tunnel segment rather than the leader. Pdi1 and drosocin are only distantly related, so the transfer is exploratory.

variants.name: Pdi1 A9Y
variants.headline: Tyrosine restored at the Api Tyr7 column

features.note: Boundary set by the point where Api and Fva1 structures become interpretable (Api 5, Fva1 7), converted to Pdi1 numbering.

rationale.hypothesis: Pdi1 lacks the A751-stacking aromatic that Api and Fva1 carry in the central segment, so adding it should tighten binding if that anchor is limiting.
rationale.edit: Introduces a tyrosine in the central segment at the position that corresponds to Api Tyr7.

observations.finding: Tyr7 stacks on A751, and para-fluoro-Phe at that position kept full activity.
observations.context: Cryo-EM geometry and Api137 derivatives.

observations.finding: A751 was proposed as the initial tunnel anchor, and the peptide was cross-linked to nearby proteins through a Tyr7 analogue.
observations.context: Cryo-EM, MD and photo-cross-linking.

observations.finding: Fva1, with a tyrosine in this column, was among the most potent peptides, though the authors favour uptake as the reason.
observations.context: Peptide panel.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference. No change in binding would indicate that Pdi1 uses other central-segment contacts, such as Pro10 or Ile11.
rationale.uncertainty: The column assignment depends on an ungapped alignment in which Pdi1 Pro10-Ile11 and Api Ile8-Pro9 are transposed. Tyr adds hydrophobicity, which can raise nonspecific association, and a chymotrypsin site.
